record.prompt: I'm about to add a server-streaming endpoint to price-feed that pushes price ticks to the trading dashboards. Some dashboards sit on flaky office Wi-Fi. What should I configure so one sluggish dashboard can't make the server balloon? Just advise, no code yet.

record.final_answer:
Read the repo — `server.py` is a unary Thistlewire app, and Thistlewire isn't installed in this environment and the README doesn't document its streaming config, so I can't give you exact option names. Here's what to set, and why, in the order that matters:

The real risk is per-subscriber buffering
- Don't give each dashboard its own queue of ticks. One slow reader with an unbounded queue is what balloons. Structure the fan-out as a per-symbol latest-value ring buffer (or per-symbol broadcast) that subscribers read via a cursor. Then memory is O(symbols), not O(subscribers × backlog).
- For price ticks specifically, conflate: a slow dashboard should get the newest price per symbol, skipping intermediate ticks, not a replay. Carry a sequence number per symbol so it can detect gaps and refetch a snapshot on reconnect.

If the library forces a per-subscriber queue
- Hard-cap it — a few hundred messages, or ~1-2 seconds of ticks, whichever is smaller.
- Policy: drop-oldest (conflate), never block the producer, never grow. Blocking the producer serially couples every dashboard to the slowest one; growing is the memory leak.
- On overflow, either coalesce or close the stream with a retryable status. Don't hold the connection open with a growing backlog.

Transport-level backpressure
- Keep HTTP/2 flow-control windows modest. The per-stream window is your natural bound; if you tune it up into the megabytes, you've just re-enabled the ballooning at the transport layer.
- Set a per-send write deadline (1-5s is generous for a tick-sized message). If it can't drain, kill the stream rather than hold the buffer.
- Cap max concurrent streams per connection and per client, so one dashboard opening 50 tabs can't multiply the buffers. Cap subscribers per client too.

Flaky Wi-Fi needs reaping, not patience
- Server keepalive: ping every ~10-20s with a ~5-10s timeout. Without it, a dashboard that vanished holds its buffer until TCP gives up — minutes.
- Treat slow-consumer eviction as normal: disconnect, let it reconnect, send a fresh snapshot. Dashboards don't need tick-by-tick continuity.

Also worth doing
- Batch/coalesce ticks into ~50-100ms frames instead of one message per tick — fewer writes, less per-message overhead across many subscribers.
- Expose per-stream gauges: queue depth, send-block time, eviction count. Alert on evictions so "flaky Wi-Fi" is visible rather than mysterious.
- Test it: a client that reads a little then stalls must leave server RSS flat and producer latency unchanged.

If you can point me at Thistlewire's docs or install it (`thistlewire` isn't importable here), I can map these onto its actual settings.
